newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO telecom pact talks said hanging in balance.
newsitem.headline: WTO telecom pact talks said hanging in balance.

text.p: Trade diplomats said talks on a global pact on liberalising basic telecommunications were running into problems amid a tough stance by the United States.
"The situation is changing all the time, but at the moment there is only about a 50-50 chance of a deal," said one key source close to the negotiations.
Another said the U.S. was "pushing the barrier very high", making it increasingly difficult for many of the over 60 countries now involved.
There was no immediate comment from U.S. officials, but one source said Deputy Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang was continuing "hard work" in bilateral meetings.
Late on Wednesday, Lang said the United States was working with its partners in the World Trade Organisation negotiations to get a deal by the February 15 deadline.
But he said improvements in offers made by other countries were still needed.
"It could be that the U.S. is simply playing hardball to get the best deal it can," said one envoy.
Diplomats said one sign of whether Washington sensed a deal was possible would be a decision to send Trade Representative Charlene Barshevsky to Geneva.
U.S. sources said no such move had yet been decided.
The European Union has set a meeting of telecommunications and other ministers with interests in the talks from its 15 member states for Friday evening in Geneva.
